properties.description:
One more job in release.yml, which already builds a per-platform binary matrix (linux-x86_64, macos-arm64, macos-x86_64) and packages the consumer kit.

Builds for linux/amd64 (and linux/arm64 if consumers may land on arm hosts), tags the image with the version already in [workspace.package] so a consumer pins rather than chasing latest, publishes to a registry the consumer can pull from, and runs as a non-root user with the mounted data volume writable by that uid — the commonest way a first container run fails. The image's own documentation must state plainly that reflow2 has NO authentication and must not be reachable from outside a private network.

🛑 THE CUT MUST VERIFY THE IMAGE SEPARATELY FROM THE ASSETS, AND THIS IS THE STEP WHERE THAT IS OWED. Measured 2026-09-13/14: v0.60.0 and v0.60.1 were BOTH tagged, both published all five release assets, both read `draft: false` — and NEITHER published a container image. The release object looked complete because it WAS complete, for the assets; the image is not an asset and does not appear there. Verifying the assets off the release object, which the cut already does, says nothing about it.

HOW TO VERIFY, and read the job rather than the run:

    gh run view <run> --json jobs --jq '.jobs[] | "\(.conclusion)\t\(.name)"'

The `container image` job must read `success`. Its own last step already prints
`published <IMAGE>:<VERSION>` after an `imagetools inspect`, so the log carries
the confirmation — and the image name is `ghcr.io/<owner>/<repo>/reflow2-mcp`,
which is NOT `ghcr.io/<owner>/reflow2-mcp`; guessing the shorter one 404s and
reads exactly like a missing image.

⚠️ THE WHOLE-RUN CONCLUSION IS NOT ENOUGH EITHER WAY. A run can be RED while the
assets published, because the container job fails after `publish release` has
already succeeded — that is precisely what happened twice. Read the job.

⭐ WHY THE GATE BEING RIGHT IS THE POINT: the smoke test runs BEFORE the push, so
both failures refused to ship an unverified image rather than shipping one. The
capability held; what failed was a new check inside it, and the cut had no step
that would notice the difference.

2026-10-01 — THE JOB IS NOW FOUR, AND EACH ARCHITECTURE PASSES ITS OWN GATE (#617, reflow2 PR #646; chg:the-release-publishes-one-amd64-and-arm64-index-and-names-its-digest).
· binaries adds linux-arm64, built NATIVELY on ubuntu-22.04-arm (glibc parity with linux-x86_64 and the ubuntu:22.04 base; no cross-compile, no QEMU).
· image, one job per architecture ON ITS OWN RUNNER: docker buildx build --load, docker/smoke.sh, and only then a push BY DIGEST, untagged, with the OCI labels. The per-arch native gate means an arm64 image that cannot start is stopped exactly as an amd64 one is, before anything is published.
· container image (the job name the cut reads is kept): docker/publish-index.sh composes the index with --dry-run and refuses unless it lists linux/amd64 AND linux/arm64, so a missing architecture tags nothing and :latest does not move; then creates :<version> and :latest as ONE index, reads the pushed tag back, checks it again, and outputs the index digest. Its log still says "published <IMAGE>:<VERSION>".
· publish release now NEEDS container image, requires reflow2-mcp-linux-arm64.tar.gz, and writes the image section with the index digest into the notes before it un-drafts (docker/image-release-notes.sh: between markers, appended to the cut's notes, replaced on a re-run).
🛑 THE COUPLING IS DELIBERATE: publish used to finish without the image (fact:the-cut-verified-the-assets-and-never-the-image-2026-09-14); now a release whose image failed stays a draft. "HOW TO VERIFY" above still holds: read the `container image` job. The notes now carry the digest as well.
· A workflow_dispatch with dry_run=true builds and smoke-tests everything and pushes nothing; every writing step and job is gated by `github.event_name == 'push' || inputs.dry_run == false`. To rehearse a branch: gh workflow run release.yml --ref feat/617-multi-arch-image-with-its-digest -f dry_run=true.
The sentence above saying the image's documentation must state reflow2 has NO authentication is overtaken by v0.76.0; see req:reflow2-consumable-as-an-image's 2026-10-01 note for what the image says now.
properties.name: The release workflow publishes a tagged container image alongside the binaries
